items.stem: A variable may hold a value or be nil, and you want to run code only when it has a value. Which Swift construct is designed for this?

options.rationale: Correct: if let (or guard let) safely unwraps an optional and binds the value when present.
Force unwrapping crashes if the value is nil, so it is not the safe choice.
Scope of storage has nothing to do with safely handling nil.
Loops iterate sequences; they do not unwrap a single optional.

items.explanation: Correct: if let (or guard let) safely unwraps an optional and binds the value when present.

items.stem: You assign one struct value to a new variable and change the new one. What happens to the original struct?

options.text: It is unchanged because structs are value types and are copied
options.rationale: Correct: structs have value semantics, so the copy is independent.

options.text: It also changes because both share one instance
options.rationale: That describes reference types such as classes, not structs.
Assignment does not nil out the source value.
Copying a struct is safe and does not throw.

items.explanation: Correct: structs have value semantics, so the copy is independent.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Swift protocols are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A protocol can declare required methods and properties without implementing them
options.rationale: Correct: a protocol specifies requirements that conforming types must satisfy.

options.text: A protocol extension can provide default method implementations
options.rationale: Correct: protocol extensions supply shared default behaviour.

options.text: A type may conform to only one protocol at a time
options.rationale: A type can conform to many protocols.

options.text: Protocols can only be adopted by classes
options.rationale: Structs and enums can also conform to protocols.

items.explanation: Correct: a protocol specifies requirements that conforming types must satisfy.; Correct: protocol extensions supply shared default behaviour.
